title: Conversation Velocity — hypotheses & mini-PRD
content:
Goal:
Short hypothesis-driven effort to explore features that increase perceived conversation "velocity" — i.e., make multi-turn chat feel faster and more fluid for end users while keeping per-session cost bounded. Not about raw throughput only; includes UX tactics and server-side optimizations that reduce waiting, unnecessary tokens, and repeated work across turns.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Customers building chat assistants report users dropping off in long sessions because responses feel slow or the assistant repeats context-heavy memory every turn.
- Many apps need a blend: fast short-turn answers + occasional high-quality long-form generation. We lack a lightweight toolkit for adaptive fidelity and preemptive processing that can be toggled per-route.

Success metrics (initial):
- Perceived response latency reduction (user-measured): % users reporting slowness in experiments — target 30% relative improvement on long sessions.
- 90th percentile server response time for interactive turns (<= target_ms TBD per model).
- Token cost per session reduction (median) without degrading task success by > 5% on key eval prompts.
- Engagement: session length increase or retention lift in A/B test.

Key concepts / primitives to explore:
1) Early partial renders + progressive completion:
   - Stream a short deterministic summary/intent ack within 50–150ms (very small model or template), then stream full generation. Improves perceived latency.
2) Adaptive fidelity profiles:
   - Route short, high-frequency turns to a trimmed prompt + smaller model or quantized variant. Switch to larger model on explicit signals (e.g., long user turn, explicit ask for details).
3) Turn-level diffing + delta prompts:
   - Compute minimal delta from prior assistant output to avoid re-sending history tokens; use cached embeddings or compressed diffs as prefix.
4) Proactive context compaction:
   - Periodically synthesize short anchors (2–3 lines) representing the last N turns for faster re-hydration. Keep full transcript in cold store.
5) Background speculative generation:
   - For anticipated follow-ups (based on intent classifier), run cheap speculative responses to have a warm candidate ready. Cancel/merge if user input diverges.

Initial user stories (rough):
- As a developer, I want a configurable "velocity" profile per route so I can trade latency vs depth for different product flows (quick-reply vs deep-chat).
- As a user, I want the assistant to give a fast short answer and then expand if I ask for more—so I don't wait for long answers when I only need a quick pointer.
- As an SRE, I want telemetry hooks to track which fidelity profile was used per request and the cost delta, so we can optimize allocations and billing.

Non-goals (for first pass):
- Do not attempt to rewrite the entire session store architecture. Aim for incremental features built atop existing session caching.
- Not a personalization project (though later features may benefit).

Proposed minimal MVP surface (developer-facing):
- New request param: velocity_profile: [fast, balanced, thorough] (string).
- Server-side behavior mapping (configurable per API key/route):
   - fast => small model / truncated prompt / early partial render template
   - balanced => mid model + prefix compaction
   - thorough => large model + full history
- Telemetry events: velocity.profile, velocity.switch_reason, speculative.hit/miss, anchor.created.
- Opt-in config in Console: default profile per route + soft-fallback logic.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Implement profile parameter in hosted API + routing logic to model variants.
- Implement prefix compaction prototype: anchor creation and use for a single-route example.
- Simple streaming early-ack template implemented for the chat SDK.
- Dashboard telemetry surfaced for sample customers showing profile usage and cost delta.

Low-level implementation notes / technical approach:
- Early-ack: lightweight deterministic template sent before model invocation; orchestrate by writing to response stream immediately and launching generation async. This is mostly a middleware change.
- Compact anchors: run a small-summarization micro-model (could be same small open model) every N turns or when token window > threshold. Store anchor in session cache with pointer. Anchor length target: 20–80 tokens.
- Delta prompts: compute sentence-level diff client-side or server-side via a cheap hashing of last assistant text; only send user deltas plus anchor to model. Need to handle hallucination risk.
- Speculative generation: use cheap model to generate candidate completions. If user input arrives and matches predicted intent (classifier threshold), return cached candidate with finalization via larger model if needed. Important to cancel tokens generation where possible to save cost.

Telemetry / experiments design:
- Track per-turn: timeToFirstByte (for early-ack), fullCompletionTime, modelUsed, tokensSent, tokensGenerated, sessionLength, userAction (accepted, asked follow-up, corrected).
- Run A/B with 10k sessions baseline vs velocity_profile=balanced. Key evals: perceived latency survey + task success automated tests.

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: anchor/summarization may drop critical context causing degraded accuracy. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, automatic fallbacks to full history on low-confidence outputs.
- Risk: billing confusion if token cost savings are marginal vs developer expectations. Need clear console reporting and sampling.
- Speculative generation could double cost if not carefully pruned. Must prototype hit-rate & cancellation logic.

Spike tasks (first 2 weeks):
- Spike A: implement early-ack middleware and measure TTFB improvement on sample routes. Owner: Darren.
- Spike B: prototype anchor summarizer (small model) + cache integration; measure token reduction and accuracy variation. Owner: Lena.
- Spike C: build simple intent predictor for speculative generation; estimate speculative hit rate. Owner: Noah.

Rollout and gradations:
- Alpha: internal customers and power users opt-in; telemetry-only mode for other devs.
- Beta: enable default profile per route in console for select orgs.
- GA: expose in pricing matrix if stable cost improvements established; document trade-offs in API docs and console.

Notes / todo (personal):
- Link to past experiments: find notes from "session-resume" and "context-eviction" docs to avoid redoing work.
- Talk to Console PM about UI for profile toggles + examples gallery.
- Check infra limits for running additional summarizer jobs — open with infra team.

Quick sketch of API example (pseudo):
POST /v1/chat/completions
body: { model: "gpt-like-large-v1", messages: [...], velocity_profile: "fast", speculative: true }
Response: stream -> { early_ack: "Thinking… here’s a pointer:", then full chunks }

References / inspiration:
- Mobile UX patterns: perceived latency vs actual latency (fast first paint analog).
- Some academic work on speculative decoding and synchronous/asynchronous hybrid responses.

Bottom line: this is a cross-cutting effort (runtime + session store + console + SDK). Start with low-friction primitives (early-ack + anchor compaction) to get UX wins before investing in speculative generation.

Draft owner: Darren Liu — will iterate after spike results and quick internal playtest.
